nodes.title: TAXONOMY
nodes.body:
Common Name: Atlantic Cutlassfish
Scientific Name: Trichiurus lepturus

nodes.title: Classification
nodes.body:
Phylum: Chordata
	Class: Osteichthyes
	Order: Perciformes
	Family: Trichiuridae

nodes.title: Other Common Names
nodes.body:
Ribbonfish (327)

Other:	Reference for Scientific Name (Linneaus 1758)
	Reference for Classification (1914)

nodes.title: VALUE & STATUS
nodes.body:
Commercial:  Some commercial value in the Caribbean mainly Cuba, Jamaica and Venezuela (2325).
Recreational:  Small Trichiurus are used for trolling bait for kingfish (327).
Ecological:  Seasonally one of the most abundant estuarine predators within the Indian River Lagoon (Gilmore pers. obs.)
Indicator:  Not known

nodes.title: GEOGRAPHIC RANGE
nodes.body:
Overall: Found in tropical and warm temperate waters of the world, except for the eastern Pacific where found only from Mexico to Panama (2325 327).  In the western Atlantic it is found from Cape Cod to Northern Gulf of Mexico and Argentina (788 2325 327).
Within Study Area:  Found throughout the Indian River Lagoon (2320 848 993 1814).
Migrations and Movements:
Trichiurus is a nocturnal vertical migrator, remaining on the bottom during the day and moving to the surface at night.   Also may move off shore in the fall (2321).
Life Mode:  A benthopelagic, euryhaline, vertically migrating predatory fish of neritic and estuarine waters.

nodes.title: Habitat Type
nodes.body: Mostly benthopelagic or bottom-living and pelagic.  Can be found on continental shelf and slope to 500 m or in shallow coastal areas, estuaries and bays with muddy bottom (2325 2321).

nodes.title: Physical/Chemical
nodes.body: Has been collected in water temperatures as low as 16.5 degrees C (1814).  Salinity range from 4.5 ppt ? seawater, but associated with salinity above 16 ppt (1814 2321).

nodes.title: Reproductive Mode
nodes.body:
Gonochoristic, oviparous, iteroparous.
Mating/Spawning::
Spawning occurs offshore at depths greater than 46 m (2321).  Spawns off the Florida coast April - May and July - December (Herrema 1985).

nodes.title: GROWTH
nodes.body:
Egg:    Eggs are pelagic with a diameter of 1.7 - 1.9 mm (2321).
Larvae:  Hatch as yolk-sac larvae at 5.5 - 6.5 mm.   Reaches 7 mm in 3 days along with yolk-sac absorption.  Larval stage is from 7.0 - 59 mm (2321).
Juvenile:  Juvenile stage 59-240 mm (2321).
Adult:  Trichiurus reaches 250 mm by the end of the first year. After three years can reach 700 mm in Gulf of Mexico.  In the northwest African population Trichiurus can reach 470 mm (47 cm) in the first year and reach 1400 mm (140 cm) in 8 years (2321). Ten to 40% of the population can reach maturity in one year and all of the population is mature by 5 years (2321).

nodes.title: FOOD HABITS
nodes.body: Feeds mainly on fish and sometimes on crustaceans and cephalopods (2321 2324).

nodes.title: ECOLOGICAL INTERACTIONS
nodes.body:
Predation: Large schools of cutlass fish migrate seasonally (spring-summer) through the Indian River Lagoon preying on a variety of fishes (RGG pers. obs.).
Factors Influencing Populations:  Cutlass fish are in turn consumed by tarpon, Megalops atlanticus and are caught by recreational fisherman (2323).
